body_text:
Archimedean property. For every real number $x$ there exists a
natural number $n$ with $n>x$. Equivalently, for every
$\epsilon>0$ there exists $n\in\mathbb{N}$ with $0<1/n<\epsilon$.
Although this property is often treated as obvious, it follows
from completeness and excludes infinitely large or positive
infinitesimal real numbers.
